title: Settings manifest: a toggle cannot declare a confirmation before it is turned off, so Setup turns off email and password sign-in without asking
body:
domain:ui#3 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbPN5UYMnBaNJPJWfG

Ruled: 6657805240 · letter A (`confirmOffText: I18nLabel`, toggle specifiers only) · 2026-11-05T12:18Z
Ruling-ref: 6657805240

Filed by the `domain:ui#3` seat from #30299 (Wanted item 1, second half), ruled out of PR #30413 (seat ruling A on the card thread; os-dev-report 6655442656). Carrier: `domain:spec` first (the key), then `domain:ui` (honouring it).

## Observed

- #30299 Wanted: Setup "asks for confirmation before turning off email and password even when another method exists ('people who sign in with a password will need another way in')".
- The Setup settings page is a generic renderer of the settings manifest. A toggle specifier has no confirmation key, so there is no declarative way to ask. Hard-coding `auth.email_password_enabled` in the renderer was ruled out (domain knowledge in a generic renderer).
- The server already refuses a save that leaves no sign-in method (#30202, PR #30298); this card is about the case where another method exists.

## Wanted

- A settings-manifest key on toggle specifiers that declares a confirmation shown when the value changes to off (shape suggestion from the card thread: `confirmOff: I18nLabel`, or `confirm: { when: false, text }`; the spec lane chooses).
- The auth manifest declares it on `email_password_enabled` with the sentence above.
- The console's settings page honours it before save.

## Related

- The same renderer ignores `confirmText` already declared on `action_button` handlers → separate card (filed alongside this one).

Refs: #30299
Dedupe words: confirmOff, toggle confirm, settings manifest confirmation, email_password_enabled confirm
